exposure: homozygous mutation (c.653C>T) in exon 6 of STAR gene
outcome: cholestatic jaundice (conjugated hyperbilirubinemia, elevated liver enzymes)
decreased levels of cortisol and sex hormones
normalization of bilirubin and liver enzymes
cohort: Two sisters, aged 30 and 60 days, presented with conjugated hyperbilirubinemia, elevated liver enzymes, and adrenal insufficiency, and were diagnosed with Lipoid Congenital Adrenal Hyperplasia.
finding: Lipoid adrenal hyperplasia should be considered as a rare cause of cholestasis with adrenal insufficiency in patients, and appropriate treatment can lead to normalization of liver enzymes and bilirubin levels.
